blocks.passage:
We live in an age of constant interruption. Notifications, messages, emails and meetings compete for our attention every few minutes. Research consistently shows that, after an interruption, it takes several minutes to return to the same depth of focus — and most of us are interrupted long before those minutes pass.

The most productive professionals protect their attention like a scarce resource. They block time for deep work. They turn off notifications during that time. They make themselves genuinely unavailable for two or three hours a day — not because they don't care about their colleagues, but because they care about doing good work.

It is worth being honest: you cannot be everywhere, all the time, and still produce your best thinking. Choosing what not to do is often more valuable than doing more. Every hour protected for focus is an hour multiplied by its quality.

options: It takes several minutes to return to the same depth of focus
items.why: "after an interruption, it takes several minutes to return to the same depth of focus."

options: As a scarce resource to protect
items.why: "protect their attention like a scarce resource."

items.q: Why do they make themselves unavailable for a few hours a day?
options: Because they don't care about colleagues
Because they care about doing good work
items.why: "not because they don't care about their colleagues, but because they care about doing good work."

items.q: What does the text say is often more valuable than doing more?
items.why: "Choosing what not to do is often more valuable than doing more."

options: focused time is worth more than the same time interrupted
items.why: Inferência: uma hora protegida rende mais do que uma hora fragmentada.

audio.text:
You said you feel overwhelmed, like you're busy all day but never get the real work done. That's incredibly common, and it's usually not about working harder.

Here's what I'd try. Every morning, before checking messages, block two hours for deep work — one task, no notifications, phone in a drawer. Two hours of focused work will beat a whole scattered day.

The hard part isn't the blocking; it's protecting it. People will message you, and you'll feel rude ignoring them. But most things can wait ninety minutes. You're not being unavailable because you don't care — you're doing it so you can actually think.

Also, stop trying to multitask. Switching between a report and your inbox every two minutes feels productive, but each switch costs you focus. Do one thing, finish it, then move on.

Try it for a week. Same two hours, same task first. I think you'll be surprised how much clears by lunch.

items.q: How does the colleague feel?
options: Overwhelmed — busy all day but never getting the real work done
items.why: "you feel overwhelmed, like you're busy all day but never get the real work done."

items.q: What does Emily suggest doing every morning?
options: Block two hours for deep work before checking messages
items.why: "Every morning, before checking messages, block two hours for deep work."

items.q: According to Emily, what is the hard part?
items.why: "The hard part isn't the blocking; it's protecting it."

items.q: Why does Emily tell the colleague to stop multitasking?
options: Each switch costs focus, even though it feels productive
It's faster to do everything at once
items.why: "each switch costs you focus. Do one thing, finish it, then move on."

items.q: What does Emily ask the colleague to try for a week?
options: The same two hours, same task first
items.why: "Try it for a week. Same two hours, same task first."

items.q: "She protects two hours for **deep work** each morning." Deep work is…
options: focused, undistracted work on a demanding task
items.why: Deep work = trabalho profundo, concentrado.

items.q: "Every **notification** pulls your attention away." A notification is…
options: an alert from an app or device
items.why: Notification = notificação, alerta.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Try to **block time** for the report so nothing ___ it."
items.why: O sentido do bloco de tempo é impedir interrupções (interruption).

items.q: A **context switch** is…
options: moving your attention from one task to another
items.why: Context switch = troca de contexto, custosa para o foco.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Don't try to ___ — do one thing at a time."
items.why: To multitask = fazer várias coisas ao mesmo tempo.

items.q: "I need to **buckle down** and finish this report." To buckle down means to…
items.why: Buckle down = concentrar-se e trabalhar a sério.

items.q: "Messages keep **cropping up** and breaking my focus." To crop up means to…
items.why: Crop up = surgir de repente.

items.q: "Let's **knock out** the easy tasks first." To knock out means to…
items.why: Knock out = despachar/terminar rapidamente.

items.q: "I keep getting **bogged down** in email." To be bogged down means to…
options: be stuck and slowed by something
items.why: Bogged down = atolado, preso.

items.q: "Let's **switch off** notifications for two hours." To switch off means to…
items.why: Switch off = desligar.
